title: 第94章 反戈一击，送上律师函

第94章 反戈一击，送上律师函-《重生2000：撕了协议我暴富了》

姚科长带人往后厨方向走。

陆骁跟在后面，脚步不慢。

他看见厨房区域还没完全封板，排烟管道外侧包着保护膜，目光停了一下。

许泰教他的词，终于有地方用了。

“姚科长，这里我得多说一句。”

陆骁抬手指向排烟口。

“这种老洋房改商业，最怕的就是厨房排烟。现在他们说做茶点，明天就能做私宴，后天是不是就能变成会员制餐厅？”

年轻工作人员停下笔。

姚科长也转头看向苏晚棠。

“你们这里后期到底会不会有餐饮经营？”

苏晚棠还没开口，陆骁又补了一句。

“还有会员制。表面不对散客开放，实际就是更私密的餐饮会所。附近居民怎么监督？消防怎么核定？食品安全怎么追责？”

他一口气说完，胸口那股憋着的火散了些。

这套词，许泰说得没错。

办事难，找事容易。

现场安静了几秒。

苏晚棠拿起文件。

夏若冰先一步伸手，把另一份蓝色文件夹递了过去。

“姚科长，这是藏锋接待体系和用途边界说明。”

她声音不高。

姚科长接过去。

封面上写着四行字。

非开放式餐饮。

非散客经营。

非高频翻台。

非宴席承接。

陆骁皱了下眉。

夏若冰继续说：“藏锋的主业是商务交流和茶事接待。厨房只承担茶点复热、简餐备餐、冷泡茶制备，不设置明火大炒，不做开放菜单，不对外售卖堂食。”

她翻开第二页。

“正式宴请由外部中央厨房配送。这里有供应商资质、配送温控记录模板、原料留样条款、抽检责任条款和加急配送费用上限。”

年轻工作人员看了她一眼。

这份材料不是临时凑出来的。

姚科长翻到后面。

“会员建档？”

夏若冰点头。

“每位会员建立饮品偏好、过敏源、接待禁忌档案。茶点不做现场推荐式销售，避免诱导消费，也避免超范围经营。”

陆骁终于忍不住笑了一声。

“你说得倒像那么回事。”

他上下看了夏若冰一眼。

“你以前做什么的？懂上海老房子的商业规矩吗？”

现场没人接话。

苏晚棠眉头抬起。

夏若冰手指压着文件边缘，脸色白了点。

过去三年，她听过太多这种话。

你懂什么？

你不就是卖酒的吗？

你陪客户笑一笑就行，别谈专业。

她看着陆骁。

“我不懂摆谱。”

她停了一下。

“但我懂服务场景和责任边界。”

陆骁脸上的笑僵住。

夏若冰把第三页推到姚科长面前。

Section Chief Yao led people towards the kitchen.

Lu Xiao followed, not slow.

He paused for a moment when he saw that the kitchen area had not been completely sealed, and the outside of the exhaust pipe was covered with a protective film.

The words Xu Tai taught him finally found a place to use.

"Chief Yao, I have one more thing to say here."

Lu Xiao raised his hand and pointed to the smoke vent.

"The biggest fear of this kind of old bungalow being converted into a business is the smoke from the kitchen. Now they say they will make refreshments, but they can have a private banquet tomorrow. Will they be able to turn it into a members-only restaurant the day after tomorrow?"

The young staff member stopped writing.

Section Chief Yao also turned to look at Su Wantang.

"Will you have a catering business here in the future?"

Before Su Wantang spoke, Lu Xiao added another sentence.

"There is also a membership system. It is not open to individual customers on the surface, but it is actually a more private dining club. How will nearby residents supervise it? How will the fire protection be verified? How will food safety be held accountable?"

He finished speaking in one breath, and the simmering fire in his chest dissipated a little.

Xu Tai is right about this set of words.

It's hard to do things, but easy to find things.

The scene was quiet for a few seconds.

Su Wantang picked up the document.

Xia Ruobing reached out first and handed over another blue folder.

"Chief Yao, this is a description of Zangfeng's reception system and usage boundaries."

Her voice is not high.

Section Chief Yao took it.

There are four lines of words written on the cover.

Not open for dining.

Not operated by individual customers.

Non-high frequency turning.

Not accepted for banquets.

Lu Xiao frowned.

Xia Ruobing continued: "Zangfeng's main business is business exchanges and tea receptions. The kitchen is only responsible for reheating refreshments, preparing light meals, and preparing cold brewed tea. There is no open fire for stir-frying, no open menu, and no dine-in sales."

She turned to the second page.

"Formal banquets are delivered from an external central kitchen. Here are supplier qualifications, delivery temperature control record templates, raw material sample retention terms, random inspection liability terms and expedited delivery fee caps."

The young staff member glanced at her.

This material was not improvised.

Section Chief Yao turned to the back.

"Member creation?"

Xia Ruobing nodded.

"Each member establishes a file of drink preferences, allergens, and reception taboos. Refreshments are not sold through on-site recommendation to avoid inducing consumption and operating beyond the scope."

Lu Xiao finally couldn't help laughing.

"That's what you said."

He glanced at Xia Ruobing up and down.

"What did you do before? Do you understand the business rules of Shanghai's old houses?"

No one answered the call.

Su Wantang raised his eyebrows.

Xia Ruobing pressed her fingers on the edge of the document and turned a little pale.

She had heard this too much in the past three years.

What do you know?

Aren’t you a wine seller?

Just smile with your customers and don't talk about professionalism.

She looked at Lu Xiao.

"I don't know how to stage things."

She paused.

“But I understand service scenarios and boundaries of responsibility.”

The smile on Lu Xiao's face froze.

Xia Ruobing pushed the third page in front of Section Chief Yao.
